Simulate independent survey programs on a shared population

Source: R/sim_programs.R
sim_surveys.Rd

Each program observes the original rounded annual population snapshot, including after sim_fisheries(). Surveys do not deplete another program's population or consume the fishing mortality budget.

sim_surveys(sim, ..., n_sims = NULL)

Arguments

sim

A simulation list returned by sim_distribution() or sim_fisheries().

...

Named sim_survey_spec configurations created with sim_survey() without sim. Names must be unique and nonempty.

n_sims

Common replicate count; NULL inherits existing batch metadata, otherwise one. Do not supply counts inside configurations.

Value

A simulation list with common replicates and named survey_programs. Use select_survey() to create a standard single-survey view for existing analyses and plots. Top-level stale survey observations and analyses are cleared.

Details

Configurations run in canonical name order using caller-controlled randomness. All programs' locations and catches are generated before any program's biological subsampling, so changing sampling caps does not change another program's locations or catches. Mutable tables are isolated between programs.

The common population is stored once. Each program retains abundance available to the survey across the full grid (I, I_at_length, and keyed spatial sp_I), set details, biological samples, summaries, evaluated catchability, its eligible survey frame when known, and its configuration. The existing surveys design table used by test_surveys() is preserved. Repeated calls replace program results with a fresh simulation; they do not append or replay earlier programs.

See also

vignette("fisheries", package = "SimSurvey") for multiple survey programs and program extraction. strat_error() compares estimates with abundance after applying q at age or length, across the full grid by default or within each intended survey footprint.

Examples

survey_A <- sim_survey(q = sim_logistic(), q_by = "age")
survey_B <- sim_survey(q = sim_logistic(x50 = 30), q_by = "length")
# population |> sim_surveys(survey_A = survey_A, survey_B = survey_B)
